summary: Receives UDP or multicast UDP data from remote computers, appends incoming data to a DAT table, and can run callbacks for received messages.

key_params.name: address
key_params.note: Multicast address to listen on when multicast is selected

key_params.name: shared
key_params.note: Share the network connection with compatible DATs

key_params.name: format
key_params.note: Parse incoming data one row per byte, line, or message

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Callback DAT executed for each incoming message

key_params.name: clamp
key_params.note: Limit output rows instead of allowing unlimited accumulation

key_params.name: maxlines
key_params.note: Maximum retained rows when clamping is enabled

key_params.name: bytes
key_params.note: Output raw message bytes in a separate column

key_params.name: executeloc
key_params.note: Choose the execution context for received-data callbacks

key_params.name: fromop
key_params.note: Operator path used when Execute from is set to Specified Operator

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: UDP has no delivery, ordering, or connection guarantee; design protocols to tolerate missing packets.
The send command cannot reply until a message has been received because the DAT has no peer address yet.
In multicast mode, replies go directly to the originator of the last received multicast message.
Row/Callback Format changes table shape and callback granularity, so choose per-message for packet protocols.
Windows firewall or OS network permissions can prevent packets from arriving.
key_concepts: UDP In DAT receives UDP or multicast UDP data and appends received messages to a DAT table.
It captures messages without transport-level delivery guarantees or persistent queuing.
Replies through send methods only work after a sender address has been learned from received data.
Callbacks and clamp settings control per-message handling and bounded output history.
